thread.title: How Bad Could the Next Tariffs Hurt Apple? Depends Whom You Ask

title: How Bad Could the Next Tariffs Hurt Apple? Depends Whom You Ask
text:
How Bad Could the Next Tariffs Hurt Apple? By Updated Nov. 30, 2018 4:23 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Text size
A 10% tariff on Apple (AAPL) iPhones made in China could mean a hit to next year’s earnings. How big a hit? Depends whom you ask.
Analysts are chiming in following statements made earlier this week by President Donald Trump suggesting that the company’s phones and laptops might be added to a list of goods covered by tariffs next year.
“I can make it 10% and people could stand that very easily,” Trump told The Wall Street Journal . Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping at the G-20 summit that begins today in Buenos Aires.
Of course, it’s not even clear how Apple might respond to such a move. It could shift some manufacturing outside of China. It could raise prices. Or it could absorb the tariffs.
In a Friday note, JP Morgan ’s Samik Chatterjee , who has an Overweight rating and a $266 price target—16% above FactSet’s $230 average—on Apple shares, wrote, “Based on our estimate that roughly a quarter of iPhone shipments directed to the U.S. would be impacted by this tariff, we believe Apple is more likely to refrain from taking pricing actions to pass on the tariff impact to U.S. consumers.” Newsletter Sign-up
Chatterjee estimates a 45-cent hit to his current full-year (ending September 2019) earnings-per-share estimate of $13.55, representing about a 3.3% knock, if that happens. FactSet’s current average EPS estimate is $13.36.
Morgan Stanley ’s Katy Huberty expects Apple to either pass any tariff costs to the consumer via pricing or absorb them, “both of which are value destructive from the perspective of an Apple shareholder.” Recommended Reading
